properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 6:58AM EDT until October 15 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Columbia SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in South
Carolina...

Congaree River At Congaree River at Columbia affecting Lexington
and Richland Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Congaree River at Congaree River at Columbia.

* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Flooding occurs on parts of the Cayce and
West Columbia Riverwalk. At 12.5 feet, Most of the West Columbia
Riverwalk between Gervais Street and SC 12 is underwater. At 14.0
feet, Roads in low lying areas and swampland downstream from
Columbia become flooded. Most of the Cayce and West Columbia
Riverwalk is flooded. At 16.0 feet, Old State Road below Cayce
becomes flooded. At 6.5 feet, The lowest parts of the West Columbia
Riverwalk between Gervais Street and SC 12 begin to flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:00 AM EDT Monday the stage was 9.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 19.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 14.8 feet
early tomorrow afternoon.
- Action stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 700 PM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 12 at 3:51AM PDT until October 12 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, increased risk of rip currents and sneaker waves
expected with breaking waves up to 16 feet.

* WHERE...San Francisco, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern
Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 3 PM PDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical. Dangerous conditions are
forecast along the shoreline. Hazards include sneaker waves,
strong rip currents, and large breaking waves.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at
12:46 PM Monday 10/12, and 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW)
at 1:14 PM Tuesday 10/13. These predictions include up to 1.5
ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda
Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against the
current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If
unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 12 at 3:02AM PDT until October 12 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...A very long period westerly swell will increase the
threat of sneaker waves.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Through this evening. The risk will increase as winds
weaken.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

NWSheadline: BEACH HAZARDS STATEMENT NOW IN EFFECT THROUGH THIS EVENING

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 3:57AM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA... Yuma, Kit Carson, Cheyenne KS and Dundy
counties.

* TIMING... 9 AM MDT to 4 PM MDT (10 AM MDT to 5 PM CDT). Duration
of strong winds and low humidities together expected to be 1 to
2 hours.

* WINDS... West southwesterly 15 to 30 mph in the morning,
decreasing through the afternoon.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY... Falling to 10 to 15 percent in the
afternoon.

* TEMPERATURES... Lower to mid 80s.

* FUELS... Fuels will promote fire spread if fires were to
develop.

* FIRE DANGER...Lowest humidities will overlap with stronger
winds for an hour or two this afternoon. While not expected to
be widespread or persistent, these conditions could make
controlling any fire difficult.

Outdoor burning and activities that cause open sparks or flames
are discouraged. Fire and emergency officials should be aware that
weather conditions will be favorable for the development of grass
and crop fires.

properties.headline: Hazardous Seas Warning issued October 12 at 2:56AM PDT until October 12 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Very steep and hazardous seas 10 to 14 feet and north
winds 20 to 25 kt with gusts up to 35 kt expected.

* WHERE...Waters from Cape Mendocino to Pt. Arena CA from 10 to
60 nm.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or cause
damage to vessels.
properties.instruction:

should prepare for rough seas and consider remaining in port
until hazardous seas subside.

properties.areaDesc: Clinton, IA; Scott, IA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 12 at 4:47AM CDT until October 12 at 11:00PM CDT by NWS Quad Cities IA IL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Iowa...

Wapsipinicon River near De Witt 4S affecting Scott and Clinton
Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Wapsipinicon River near De Witt 4S.

* WHEN...Until this evening.

* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet, water affects County Road E63 north of the
river near Toronto and affects the lowest roads in Buena Vista.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:30 AM CDT Monday the stage was 11.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this morning and continue falling to 8.1 feet Sunday, October 18.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

The next statement will be issued by this evening.
